hints: Look closely at the numbers in each box in diagram A. Remember that with negative values, -22 is higher than -36, just like -2 is higher than -5.
Net osmosis is always from higher water potential (less negative) to lower water potential (more negative) across each touching wall. Test each arrow one by one.
walkthrough:
**Recall the osmosis rule**

Think like water. Water always moves down its water potential gradient to try to reach equilibrium.

Key rule:
$$\text{net water movement: higher } \Psi \text{ (less negative) } \rightarrow \text{ lower } \Psi \text{ (more negative)}$$

**Test all arrows in diagram A**

Top right cell is $\Psi = -22$ kPa. This is the highest value of the four, so water should leave it in all directions. It does: to $-40$, to $-36$ and to $-33$.

Then check the bottom row: $-33 \rightarrow -36$ is correct because $-33 > -36$. And $-36 \rightarrow -40$ is correct because $-36 > -40$.

**Conclude the correct pattern**

Every single arrow in A follows high to low water potential. The other diagrams each contain at least one arrow going from low to high, which is impossible for net osmosis. So A is the only fully correct diagram.

options.A: All five arrows go from higher to lower Psi, for example -22 to -40, -22 to -36, -22 to -33, -33 to -36, and -36 to -40. This is exactly correct for net osmosis.
options.B: Contains reversed arrows, for example -22 to -16 and -38 to -32 both go from lower to higher water potential, which cannot be net osmosis.
options.C: Contains reversed arrows, for example -33 to -25 goes from lower to higher, and -33 to -33 shows movement where there is no gradient.
options.D: Almost correct but the bottom arrow goes from -27 to -24, which is lower to higher. Net movement should be -24 to -27 instead.
